root_cause_label: Agent validated fasttext with superficial import/attribute checks but never called model.predict() on a single string, so the NumPy 2.x incompatibility in FastText.py (np.array with copy=False) was never triggered and the required patch was never applied
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent installed fasttext into a non-system pip environment and validated only import/method-presence rather than exercising predict(), so it missed the NumPy 2.x crash and never applied the required np.asarray patch.
t_err_evidence: Step 4: agent ran 'pip3 install fasttext' using /opt/miniswea/bin/pip3 (non-system environment) and installed numpy 2.4.0 alongside fasttext 0.9.3, a combination known to break predict() on single strings; the agent assumed this was a global system-wide installation.
t_commit_evidence: Step 5: after observing 'FastText imported successfully', the agent declared the problem solved and shifted entirely to writing confirmation scripts; from this point all subsequent actions were superficial validation loops that never tested predict().
trigger_explanation: The agent operated under the false premise that (1) pip3 at /opt/miniswea/bin/pip3 targets the system-wide Python used by the benchmark, and (2) a successful import plus method-presence check is sufficient to confirm fasttext is working. Neither premise was verified, causing the agent to skip reproducing and patching the actual predict() failure.
forewarning_evidence: Step 3: 'which pip3' returned '/opt/miniswea/bin/pip3', clearly indicating a non-system pip path; the agent noticed but did not investigate whether this aligned with the system Python used by the benchmark.
